{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZeii2Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDFwFo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 49, "title": "Add ROMless Snatcher and SD Snatcher SCC-I sound cartridges", "body": "## Problem

The emulator supports classic Konami SCC cartridges but cannot install either original SCC-I sound cartridge. `crates/msx-core/src/scc.rs` stores four waveforms, `cartridge.rs` requires an AB-header ROM, and `Machine::step` mixes SCC only for `Mapper::KonamiScc`.

Snatcher and SD Snatcher sound cartridges supply banked RAM as well as five-channel sound. Their missing hardware restricts commercial disk workloads beyond audio alone. Neither game's execution or playability has been observed here.

## Expected outcome

Provide explicit, ROMless Snatcher and SD Snatcher 64 KiB sound-cartridge profiles through the core, Wasm and browser. Occupy existing cartridge slot 1, alongside the existing disk interface in slot 2. Implement the selected profiles' RAM banking, protection, compatible/plus sound registers and independent fifth waveform.

Keep this one coherent hardware addition. A general slot framework, simultaneous ordinary cartridge, expanded modern SCC cartridges and unrelated synthesis/timing corrections are outside scope.

## Context

- Baseline: `382499bbff3b0ba2985c0462f8946261162457aa`; clean local HEAD matches inspected GitHub main. The open Issue/PR collection is empty. Earlier [#23](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/23) and [#39](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/39) concern classic SCC and its audio continuity.
- Inspect `crates/msx-core/src/{scc.rs,cartridge.rs,lib.rs,psg.rs}`, `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs`, browser cartridge/firmware/import handling, existing SCC tests and Philips CPU fixtures. Audit assumptions that an installed cartridge always has nonempty ROM bytes or an AB boot vector.
- Pinned upstream [sound-cartridge decoding](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/MSXSCCPlusCart.cc) defines the two RAM populations, bank registers, mode register and overlay priority. [SCC synthesis/register decoding](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/sound/SCC.cc) distinguishes original SCC, SCC-I compatible mode and plus mode. Use these as behavioral evidence; independently author implementation and fixtures.
- Upstream [Snatcher](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/share/extensions/Konami_Snatcher_Sound_Cartridge.xml) and [SD Snatcher](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/share/extensions/Konami_SD-Snatcher_Sound_Cartridge.xml) configurations map only 4000h–BFFFh and require no ROM. [Upstream user documentation](https://www.msxblue.com/manual/scc_c.htm) identifies their commercial applicability; it does not establish this emulator's compatibility.
- Hardware-reference alternatives at MSXnet and NGS returned 502/403. The inspected upstream explicitly leaves underlying RAM writes beneath a readable sound overlay uncertain. Adopt its RAM-write policy provisionally, document that uncertainty and test the chosen behavior without presenting it as a physical measurement.
- Existing SCC regression tests were inspected. `docs/validation.md` and [PR #48](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/48) report 186 Rust and 102 browser passes. Inspected CI metadata marks native/build steps successful, but browser testing remains in progress. No builds or tests were executed for this handoff.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement four 8 KiB windows at 4000h–BFFFh. Snatcher populates banks 0–7; SD Snatcher populates 8–15. RAM addressing uses the low four selector bits; unpopulated banks read FFh and ignore RAM writes. Preserve full selector values for sound-enable decoding. Outside this device's range reads return FFh.
- [ ] Implement bank-register ranges 5000h–57FFh, 7000h–77FFh, 9000h–97FFh and B000h–B7FFh, plus write-only mode control at BFFEh/BFFFh with priority over RAM/sound writes. Mode bit 4 makes all windows writable RAM; otherwise bits 0/1 enable RAM writes in windows 1/2, and bit 2 enables window 3 only with bit 5 set. Window 4 otherwise remains protected. RAM-mode writes must not change bank selectors or sound registers. Cover boundary addresses and reserved bits.
- [ ] In compatible mode, selector 3 low-six-bits=3Fh exposes 9800h–9FFFh. In plus mode, selector 4 bit 7 exposes B800h–BFFFh. Implement low-byte register mirrors and the SCC-I maps: compatible four writable waves, fifth-wave readback at offsets A0h–BFh and controls at 80h–9Fh; plus five writable waves at 00h–9Fh and controls at A0h–BFh. Both use deformation offsets C0h–DFh, with SCC-I bit-7 behavior, read side effects and write protection. Compatible wave-4 writes also update wave 5; mode changes alone must not destroy independently programmed fifth-wave data.
- [ ] Mix and clock the installed device independently of overlay/slot visibility. Verify independent voice-4/5 PCM in plus mode, compatible shared-wave updates, masks, periods, signed DAC output, chunk invariance, hidden-window phase continuity and simultaneous PSG mixing. Preserve existing classic SCC behavior and its regressions. Existing digital synthesis approximations may remain documented.
- [ ] Add transactional explicit installation/removal without fabricated ROM headers, BIOS traps or automatic game detection. Installation/replacement and accessory removal restart the selected firmware while retaining system ROMs, disk interface and mounted/modified media. Slot 1 has one occupant; reuse existing SRAM-save safeguards before replacing an ordinary cartridge. Failed requests and stale imports preserve the running session. Expose active profile and removal in advanced browser controls.
- [ ] Distinguish insertion from hardware reset. Reset retains accessory RAM, restores selectors 0/1/2/3 and compatible mode, disables sound and clears deformation/queued PCM; retain SCC-I wave/period/volume state consistently with the pinned reset model. Document deterministic insertion initialization as emulator policy. Removal/replacement discards volatile RAM. Preserve existing cartridge-clearing behavior for model changes and bundled-firmware controls; external firmware application and disk boot retain the accessory. Cover each transition explicitly and keep ordinary-cartridge behavior unchanged.
- [ ] Add independent native bank/protection traces for both profiles on both models: all populated/unpopulated banks, selector aliases, window isolation, disabled writes, RAM/bank-mode transitions, mode-register priority and overlay reads/writes. Use fixed expected bytes and addresses rather than production helpers as the oracle. Label the provisional overlay-write expectation separately.
- [ ] Extend original CPU-executed fixtures to load a disk sector, program/read accessory RAM through real slot and memory accesses, execute code copied into that RAM, and exercise both sound modes while the Philips disk interface remains installed. Assert an independently expected result/trace and distinct fifth-channel PCM. Cover MSX1/MSX2 and preserve MSX2 sub-ROM/mapper access. Proprietary firmware and gameplay are unnecessary.
- [ ] Add compiled-Wasm browser checks at `/` and `/msx-rust/` for both profiles, installation/status, CPU fixture output and PCM, reset/removal/replacement, failed/stale operations and retained disk/firmware state. Preserve audio activation/mute/pause, disk ownership/export, existing SRAM persistence and local-only firmware handling.
- [ ] Update affected hardware/help/provenance documentation and independently authored fixture licensing. Before merge, the Coordinator runs and reports `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`, using documented dependency setup. Complete source-Issue/full-diff review and resolve blocking findings. Distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks; fixture success does not establish commercial playability.

## Optional validation

Compare original bank/register traces and steady-state PCM with the pinned upstream profiles. Record physical or already lawfully available software observations if available. These comparisons have not been performed and are not merge prerequisites. Exact DAC-update latency, analog effects and physical confirmation of overlay RAM writes remain limitations.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
